questions.question: A motorboat journeys 32 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 7 hours. In another journey along the same river, it covers 40 km upstream and 48 km downstream in 9 hours. Find the speed of the motorboat in still water.
questions.title: Motorboat: speed in still water (boats & streams)

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: If u = time to cover 1 km upstream, d = time to cover 1 km downstream, set up two linear equations from the two journeys.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
- 32u + 36d = 7 ... (i)
- 40u + 48d = 9 ... (ii)
Multiply (i) by 1.25: 40u + 45d = 8.75. Subtract from (ii): 3d = 0.25 → d = 1/12 (downstream speed = 12 km/hr).
Substitute into (i): 32u + 3 = 7 → u = 1/8 (upstream speed = 8 km/hr).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Speed in still water = (upstream + downstream)/2 = (8+12)/2 = **10 km/hr**.

questions.question: A man can row at 5 km/hr in still water. If the velocity of the current is 1 km/hr and it takes him 1 hour to row to a place and come back, how far is the place?
questions.title: Rowing — distance to a place and back

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Still-water speed = 5 km/hr, current = 1 km/hr, total round-trip time = 1 hr.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: Upstream speed = 4 km/hr, downstream speed = 6 km/hr. Let distance = x: x/4 + x/6 = 1 → (3x+2x)/12 = 1 → 5x = 12 → x = 2.4.

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 80 days. He works at it for 10 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 42 days. In how much time will A and B, working together, finish the work?
questions.title: Work & time — A and B together

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
A's rate = 1/80 per day. A works 10 days → completes 10/80 = 1/8. Remaining 7/8 done by B in 42 days → B's rate = (7/8)/42 = 1/48 per day.
Combined rate = 1/80 + 1/48. LCM(80,48) = 240 → 3/240 + 5/240 = 8/240 = 1/30.

questions.question: Determine the total number of digits contained in the expansion of five raised to the power of twenty, given that log base ten of two is equal to 0.3010.
questions.title: Digits in 5²⁰

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Number of digits = ⌊n·log₁₀(base)⌋ + 1. log₁₀5 = 1 − log₁₀2 = 1 − 0.3010 = 0.6990.
20 × 0.6990 = 13.98 → floor = 13 → digits = 13 + 1.

questions.question: If 4 men and 6 women can complete a specific piece of work in 8 days, while 3 men and 7 women can complete the same work in 10 days, in how many days will a group of 10 women working together complete this work?
questions.title: Men and women work rates

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
4m + 6w = 1/8 ... (i); 3m + 7w = 1/10 ... (ii) (work = 1 unit).
Multiply (i)×3: 12m+18w = 3/8. Multiply (ii)×4: 12m+28w = 2/5. Subtract: 10w = 2/5 − 3/8 = 1/40 → w = 1/400.
10 women's combined rate = 10/400 = 1/40 per day.

questions.question: The calendar for the year 2007 will be the same for the year:
questions.title: Calendar repeats — 2007

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A non-leap year's calendar repeats in the next year whose accumulated "odd days" (from the target year onward) sum to a multiple of 7, and which is also non-leap.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content: From 2007 to 2018 (i.e., years 2007–2017), leap years = 2008, 2012, 2016 (3 leap years) out of 11 years. Odd days = 8×1 + 3×2 = 14 → 14 mod 7 = 0.

questions.question: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ? 815 in 3 years and to ? 854 in 4 years. The sum is:
questions.title: Simple Interest — finding the principal

sections.label: Given
sections.content: Amount after 3 years = ₹815, amount after 4 years = ₹854.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
The difference (₹854 − ₹815 = ₹39) is exactly 1 year's interest. So 3 years' interest = 3 × 39 = ₹117.
Principal = Amount(3yr) − Interest(3yr) = 815 − 117.

questions.question: A boat covers 24 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 6 hours, while it covers 36 km upstream and 24 km downstream in 13/2 hours. The speed of the current is:
questions.title: Boat & stream — speed of current

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 24 up + 36 down in 6 hrs; 36 up + 24 down in 6.5 hrs.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Let x = 1/upstream speed, y = 1/downstream speed.
24x + 36y = 6 ... (i); 36x + 24y = 6.5 ... (ii).
×3 on (i): 72x+108y=18. ×2 on (ii): 72x+48y=13. Subtract: 60y=5 → y=1/12 → downstream=12.
From (i): 24x + 3 = 6 → x = 1/8 → upstream = 8.

questions.question: The calendar for the leap year 1896 will be a perfect day-by-day match with the calendar of which of the following future years?
questions.title: Leap year calendar repeat — 1896

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A leap-year calendar repeats after 28 years only if no non-leap century year (like 1900) falls in between. Here 1900 is not a leap year, so the 28-year shortcut (1924) fails.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Count odd days year by year from 1896: an ordinary year adds 1 odd day, a leap year adds 2.
2. From 1896 to 1907 (12 years) the leap years are 1896 and 1904 only (1900 is not leap), so odd days = 12 + 2 = 14, and 14 mod 7 = 0.
3. So 1908 starts on the same weekday as 1896, and 1908 is also a leap year.

questions.question: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock will the hands of a clock be together?
questions.title: Clock hands together between 2 and 3 o'clock

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Formula for hands to coincide after H o'clock: minutes = 60H/11 (since the minute hand gains 5.5°/min on the hour hand, and at H o'clock the hour hand leads by 30H°).

questions.question: A dishonest dealer cheats his wholesaler by taking 10% extra weight and cheats his customers by giving 10% less weight than the marked measure. If he marks up his goods by 20% above the cost price and offers a 10% discount, what is his overall profit percentage?
questions.title: Dishonest dealer — overall profit %

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Combine three effects: buying 10% extra weight, marking up 20%, giving 10% discount, and delivering 10% less weight.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Take CP = ₹1 per standard kg. He receives 1.1 kg from the wholesaler for the price of 1 kg → real cost per real kg = 1/1.1 = 10/11.
Marked price = 1.2 per nominal kg; after 10% discount, selling price = 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08 per nominal (labeled) kg.
He delivers only 0.9 kg for every labeled kg → revenue per real kg delivered = 1.08/0.9 = 1.2.
Profit % = (Revenue − Cost)/Cost × 100 = (1.2 − 10/11)/(10/11) × 100 = (1.32 − 1) × 100.

questions.question: Three pipes A, B, and C can together fill a cistern in 20 hours. If pipe A takes twice as long as B and C together to fill it, and pipe B takes thrice as long as A and C together, how many hours will pipe C alone take to fill the empty cistern?
questions.title: Pipes and cistern — time for C alone

sections.label: Given
sections.content: A+B+C together = 1/20 per hr. Time_A = 2 × Time_(B+C), Time_B = 3 × Time_(A+C).

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Let rate_(B+C) = x → rate_A = x/2. Since rate_A + x = 1/20: x/2 + x = 1/20 → 3x/2 = 1/20 → x = 1/30, so rate_A = 1/60.
Total: rate_A + rate_B + rate_C = 1/20 → rate_B + rate_C = 1/20 − 1/60 = 1/30.
Also rate_B = (rate_A + rate_C)/3 = (1/60 + c)/3 (where c = rate_C).
Substitute into rate_B + c = 1/30: (1/60+c)/3 + c = 1/30. Multiply by 3: 1/60 + c + 3c = 1/10 → 4c = 1/10 − 1/60 = 1/12 → c = 1/48.

questions.question: Reenu's age after 6 years will be three-sevenths of her father's age. 10 years ago, the ratio of their ages was 1 : 5. What is Reenu's father's age at present?
questions.title: Ages — Reenu and her father

sections.label: Given
sections.content: 10 years ago ratio = 1:5. After 6 years, Reenu = 3/7 × father.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Let 10 years ago: Reenu = x, Father = 5x. Present: Reenu = x+10, Father = 5x+10. After 6 more years: Reenu = x+16, Father = 5x+16.
(x+16) = (3/7)(5x+16) → 7x+112 = 15x+48 → 64 = 8x → x = 8.

questions.question: A sum of ? 800 amounts to ? 920 in 3 years at simple interest. If the interest rate is increased by 3%, it would amount to how much?
questions.title: Simple Interest — rate increase

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Interest = ₹120 over 3 years → rate = (120×100)/(800×3) = 5%. New rate = 5+3 = 8%.
New interest = 800×8×3/100 = 192. New amount = 800+192.

questions.question: What was the day of the week on 17th June, 1998?
questions.title: Day of the week — 17 June 1998

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Use a reference anchor date and count forward/backward using modulo-7 arithmetic.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
Jan 1, 2000 was a Saturday (known reference). 1998 and 1999 are both non-leap years (365 days each), so 730 days separate Jan 1, 1998 and Jan 1, 2000; 730 mod 7 = 2, so Jan 1, 1998 = Saturday − 2 days = Thursday.
Days from Jan 1 to June 17 (non-leap year): Jan(31)+Feb(28)+Mar(31)+Apr(30)+May(31) = 151, plus 17 = day 168 of the year, which is 167 days after Jan 1.
167 mod 7 = 6 → Thursday + 6 days = Wednesday.

questions.question: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'DIRECTOR' be arranged so that the three vowels always come together?
questions.title: Arrangements of DIRECTOR with vowels together

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
DIRECTOR = D,I,R,E,C,T,O,R (8 letters, R repeated twice). Vowels = I, E, O (3 distinct vowels).
Treat the 3 vowels as one block → 5 consonants (D,R,C,T,R) + 1 block = 6 units, with R repeated twice: arrangements = 6!/2! = 360.
Vowels inside the block can arrange in 3! = 6 ways.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 4 times itself?
questions.title: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest.

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: For Simple Interest, the growth is linear — the interest earned each year is constant.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Let Principal = P. Doubling means Amount = 2P, so Interest earned in 8 years = P.
2. This means the annual interest = P/8.
3. To become 4 times itself (Amount = 4P), the interest needed = 3P (since 4P - P = 3P).
4. Time = Interest needed ÷ annual interest = 3P ÷ (P/8) = 24.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61. What is the largest number?
questions.title: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 61. What is the

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: For any set of consecutive numbers (with a constant common difference), the average equals the middle term.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Average = middle (3rd) term = 61.
2. Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2, so the sequence is: 57, 59, 61, 63, 65.
3. The largest is the 5th term = 61 + 2×2 = 65.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 12 days and B can complete it in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need to finish the remaining work?
questions.title: A can complete a job in 12 days and B can complete it in 18

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Add the two work rates, subtract the fraction finished together, then divide what is left by B's rate alone.

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. A's rate = 1/12 per day and B's rate = 1/18 per day.
2. Together: 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 per day.
3. In 4 days they finish 4 × 5/36 = 5/9 of the job.
4. Remaining work = 1 − 5/9 = 4/9.
5. B alone needs (4/9) ÷ (1/18) = 8 days.
